about: Shared vectors for stripReasoning (src/ai/reasoning.ts and src-tauri/src/ai/reasoning.rs). Rule: tag names think, thinking, reasoning, reflection, case-insensitive, optional attributes (<think type="x">); a name followed by more letters (<thinker>) is not a tag. 1) Every closed block <name ...>...</name> (same name) is removed together with the spaces or tabs right after its closing tag. 2) An opening tag left without its closing tag: everything from it to the end is removed (unclosed = true). 3) A closing tag left with no opening tag before it (a template that pre-filled the opening tag): everything up to and including the LAST such closing tag is removed, plus the spaces or tabs after it. 4) When anything was removed, leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed; when nothing was removed the text is returned unchanged. removed = something was removed.

about_code: Added 2026-10-15 (both sides pass them; the rule is unchanged on 'cases'). Code: a closed code fence (a line of three or more backticks or tildes, closed by a later line of only at least as many of the same mark, spaces, tabs or a CR) and inline code (a backtick, then the next backtick on the same line with something between) are found first; an unclosed fence is no code. An opening or self-closing tag in code is code, not reasoning; so is a closing tag in code after an opening tag of the same name in code. Any other closing tag counts even in code, and when its code span holds only it (blanks aside) the backticks or fence lines go with it. <think/> and <think /> (a '/' right before the '>') are self-closing: an empty block, removed with the spaces or tabs after it.

about_after_block: Added 2026-10-15: a closing tag outside a block is rule 3 also after a block (an orphan; Rust and the stream filters always read it so). The page's own pass on a whole answer (stripReasoningOutsideCode in src/ai/reasoning.ts) differs here on purpose: it balances nested blocks and removes a stray closing tag after a block as a tag, its neighbours kept.
